Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). Every input to `verify_completion_evidence` is\n   therefore byte-identical to what the bare tool would read, so the verdict is identical. The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the\n   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö\n   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*\n   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore\n   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the\n   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global\n   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Right reason.\n\nThe reserved-store-id guard (`opsa_common.py:321-323`) is a genuine companion defect the Lead found while\nwriting the adapter fix: a store named `COMPLETE.json` would have written store files at the marker's own path\ninside `runs/<run_id>/`. Arm A14 confirms it is refused at config load, before `runs/` or `manifest.jsonl` exist.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Arm A9 falsified all six of the first\ngroup at once ÔÇö including flipping `readback` from `all_match` to `MISMATCH` ÔÇö and the restore completed\n**rc 0**, wrote the file, and printed `\"completion_marker\": \"verified\"`.\n\nNot a data-integrity fail-open: the restore decision rests on the digest-bound per-run manifest, the global\n`run_end`, and a per-file SHA-256 check before every write, none of which A9 can touch. The harm is that an\noperator reading `COMPLETE.json` during a real recovery ÔÇö the document this package exists to produce ÔÇö may be\nreading numbers the tool never checked, under a line that says `verified`. Two cheap remedies, either suffices:\nassert `marker[\"readback\"] == \"all_match\"` and `marker[\"run_manifest\"] == RUN_MANIFEST_NAME` (two lines beside\nthe existing `files` check at `restore.py:103-107`), or narrow the label to `\"pair_verified\"` so it claims only\nwhat was checked. The same applies to the per-run manifest's `dir`/`skipped` records, which are digest-bound but\nnever compared to the global manifest (only `file` records are, `restore.py:99-102`) ÔÇö harmless today because\nrestore replays the *global* records, worth one comment.\n\n### NIT-2 ÔÇö \"atomically\" is O_EXCL, not atomic publication; a torn marker permanently strands a good run\n`MTC_COMMAND_CENTER/tools/opsa/opsa_common.py:153-165` (`write_once_bytes`), used at `backup.py:260,278`.\nPacket ┬ğ4: \"written atomically\".\n\nThe safety property is obtained (arms A12/A13, ┬ğ1) ÔÇö no partial marker can be mistaken for a complete one. The\nresidue is the opposite failure: arm A13 shows a half-written `COMPLETE.json` leaves a run whose **data is\nintact on disk** but which `restore.py` will refuse forever, and which the tool's own writer cannot repair ÔÇö\n`write_once_bytes` raises `FileExistsError` by design, and the package has no delete primitive\n(`NoDeleteGuaranteeTests`), so nothing in OPS-A can clear the torn file. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the\n   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö\n   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*\n   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore\n   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the\n   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global\n   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Right reason.\n\nThe reserved-store-id guard (`opsa_common.py:321-323`) is a genuine companion defect the Lead found while\nwriting the adapter fix: a store named `COMPLETE.json` would have written store files at the marker's own path\ninside `runs/<run_id>/`. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:","+","+1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's","+   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated","+   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both","+   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). Every input to `verify_completion_evidence` is","+   therefore byte-identical to what the bare tool would read, so the verdict is identical. The only possible","+   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`","+   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.","+2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:","+   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts","+   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed","+   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the","+   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken","+   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with","+   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding","+   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.","+3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**","+   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces","+   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the","+   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö","+   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*","+   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore","+   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the","+   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global","+   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). Every input to `verify_completion_evidence` is\n   therefore byte-identical to what the bare tool would read, so the verdict is identical. The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the\n   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö\n   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*\n   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore\n   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the\n   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global\n   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Right reason.\n\nThe reserved-store-id guard (`opsa_common.py:321-323`) is a genuine companion defect the Lead found while\nwriting the adapter fix: a store named `COMPLETE.json` would have written store files at the marker's own path\ninside `runs/<run_id>/`. Arm A14 confirms it is refused at config load, before `runs/` or `manifest.jsonl` exist.\n\n---\n\n## 5. The harm is that an\noperator reading `COMPLETE.json` during a real recovery ÔÇö the document this package exists to produce ÔÇö may be\nreading numbers the tool never checked, under a line that says `verified`. Two cheap remedies, either suffices:\nassert `marker[\"readback\"] == \"all_match\"` and `marker[\"run_manifest\"] == RUN_MANIFEST_NAME` (two lines beside\nthe existing `files` check at `restore.py:103-107`), or narrow the label to `\"pair_verified\"` so it claims only\nwhat was checked. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the\n   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö\n   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*\n   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore\n   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the\n   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global\n   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Right reason.\n\nThe reserved-store-id guard (`opsa_common.py:321-323`) is a genuine companion defect the Lead found while\nwriting the adapter fix: a store named `COMPLETE.json` would have written store files at the marker's own path\ninside `runs/<run_id>/`. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). Every input to `verify_completion_evidence` is\n   therefore byte-identical to what the bare tool would read, so the verdict is identical. The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Contract-change blast radius\n\nConsumer sweep of the whole worktree (read-only `Grep` for `run_restore`, `select_run`, `import restore`,\n`restore.py`, `\"runs\"`, `runs/<`):\n\n| consumer | kind | effect of the stricter contract |\n|---|---|---|\n| `p030_closed_partition_backup_adapter.py:716,746` | **code** ÔÇö the only non-test caller of `restore.run_restore` anywhere | Was the blocker; fixed in slice 2/3, verified below |\n| `check_p030_closed_partition_backup_adapter.py` | test for the above | Updated in-scope; 45 OK |\n| `MTC_COMMAND_CENTER/tools/opsa/test_opsa.py` | the package's own suite | 39 OK |\n| `p030_opsa_heartbeat_adapter.py` / its checker | imports `opsa_common` only, never `restore` | unaffected; checker exit 0 |\n| `MTC_COMMAND_CENTER/11_TRIAGE/WP_P0_26_OPSA_2026-08-25/RESTORE_DRILL_EVIDENCE.md:120,152,477` | **document** ÔÇö the D026 restore-drill procedure | **left behind** ÔÇö see NIT-4 |\n| `MTC_COMMAND_CENTER/11_TRIAGE/WP_P0_26_OPSA_2026-08-25/LANE_REPORT.md:39` | document | describes \"`--latest`/`--run` selection\" ÔÇö stale prose |\n| `MTC_COMMAND_CENTER/02_MTC_BACKTEST/docs/backup_restore_runbook.md` | document | **not** a consumer ÔÇö it documents `02_MTC_BACKTEST/scripts/backup_restore.py`, an unrelated tool |\n| `IBKR_PAPER_BRIDGE/**`, `_deepseek_driver/**` | code | their `runs` are database tables / other directories; no OPS-A coupling |\n\n**No other code consumer exists on master.** `select_run` and `load_complete_marker` have no callers outside\n`restore.py` and the suite.\n\n### Is the slice-2/3 adapter resolution technically sound?\n\n`_isolated_restore_inputs` (`p030_closed_partition_backup_adapter.py:566-596`) now reads\n`runs/<run_id>/COMPLETE.json` and `RUN_MANIFEST.jsonl` with `read_bytes()`, raising\n`ValueError(\"P026 completion evidence is unavailable\")` on `OSError`, and writes the **same bytes** into the\nisolated `runs/<run_id>/`. Judgement on each of the brief's three questions:\n\n1. **Could the adapter path ever restore a run the bare `restore.py --run` would refuse?** No. The adapter's\n   isolated root carries (a) the run's marker bytes, (b) the run's per-run manifest bytes, (c) a *validated\n   snapshot* of the global manifest (`_restore_manifest_snapshot`, re-verified against the real file both\n   before and after the restore at `:723-736,753-758`). Every input to `verify_completion_evidence` is\n   therefore byte-identical to what the bare tool would read, so the verdict is identical. The only possible\n   divergence is in the strict direction: if the snapshot were ever a *subset*, `per_run_files != global_files`\n   would refuse. It cannot be more permissive, because none of the three inputs is synthesised.\n2. **Does the copied evidence keep its digest binding?** Yes, and it is fenced, not assumed:\n   `test_isolated_restore_carries_the_runs_own_completion_evidence` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1194-1261`) asserts\n   `seen[\"marker\"] == original_marker` and `seen[\"manifest\"] == original_run_manifest` **as bytes**, observed\n   from inside the patched `run_restore` call, plus `isolated_root.samefile(root/\"backups\")` is False ÔÇö so the\n   isolation the adapter exists for is still real. It then tampers the marker two ways (broken\n   `run_manifest_sha256`; a foreign `run_id`) and requires the adapter path to refuse with\n   `P026 check-only failed; restore withheld` and an **empty** target. A byte copy preserves a SHA-256 binding\n   trivially; the test proves it *is* a byte copy.\n3. **Does the mutant test still detect the isolation mutant for the right reason?**\n   `test_shared_archive_reversion_mutant_is_detected` (`check_ÔÇĞ:1153-1192`) replaces\n   `isolated_config = {**config, \"backup_root\": str(isolated_root)}` with `isolated_config = config`. Under the\n   new gate the mutant is caught earlier than before, so the test accepts a third message ÔÇö\n   **but only conditionally**: `if str(refused.exception) == \"P026 restore failed\"` it *requires*\n   `\"per-run manifest file records differ from the global manifest\"` in the captured stderr. A generic restore\n   failure will not pass it. The detection is still causally tied to the mutation: with isolation removed the\n   restore reads the *shared* archive, which the parent test mutates after validation, and the per-run/global\n   disagreement is exactly the footprint of that shared read. Right reason.\n\nThe reserved-store-id guard (`opsa_common.py:321-323`) is a genuine companion defect the Lead found while\nwriting the adapter fix: a store named `COMPLETE.json` would have written store files at the marker's own path\ninside `runs/<run_id>/`. Arm A14 confirms it is refused at config load, before `runs/` or `manifest.jsonl` exist.\n\n---\n\n## 5.
